name: Org Strategy Decision Tree
description: Five hard gates that determine whether a single-org recommendation can hold, or whether multi-org is required. Run this AFTER the scenario matrix returns 'Single Org' to validate feasibility.
source: Org Strategy And Design — Salesforce Life Sciences

gate_1.text: Are there data residency constraints? (e.g., country laws requiring local data storage)
gate_1.guidance: Check: China (must be separate org — hard requirement), Russia (data must be first written locally before export), Turkey (local unless individual consent), EU GDPR (export only to adequacy countries).

options.label: Yes — country requires local data storage

gate_2.text: Does the customer require localized governance? (independent change management, local administration)
gate_2.guidance: If local affiliates insist on controlling their own release calendars, configuration, and admin — a single org creates governance friction.

options.label: Centralized or mixed governance is acceptable

gate_3.text: Will data volumes exceed single-org thresholds?
gate_3.guidance: Thresholds: <5,000 users per org recommended, <10,000,000 records per entity per org. Risky modules at scale: Events Management (71 objects), Activity Plans, and Sample transactions. Objects with 200+ fields or ~10M records cause sync/bulk API/UI performance degradation.

options.label: Exceeds thresholds — >5K users or >10M records per entity

gate_4.text: Do time zone differences require isolated maintenance windows?
gate_4.guidance: Major regions (EMEA, APAC, Americas) may need separate maintenance windows. A single org means one maintenance schedule for all. If field force in 4+ time zones needs uninterrupted access during deployments, consider regional isolation.

gate_5.text: Are there regulatory data sharing restrictions between business units?
gate_5.guidance: Some pharma regulatory requirements prevent data sharing between divisions (e.g., Commercial vs. Medical Affairs, different therapeutic areas). If sharing rules alone cannot enforce the required separation, org isolation is needed.

options.label: Yes — regulatory restrictions require org isolation
Sharing rules can enforce required separation

rec_isolate_countries.text: Multi-Org Required — Isolate affected countries/markets into separate orgs.
rec_isolate_countries.detail: Create dedicated orgs for countries with data residency requirements. China is always a separate org. Consider regional groupings (EMEA org, APAC org) to minimize org count while meeting residency requirements.
rec_isolate_countries.next_step: Proceed to org design pattern selection (Regional Orgs vs. Country Clusters).

rec_multi_org.detail: One or more hard gates triggered. Before splitting: (1) evaluate whether splitting profiles within a single org resolves the issue (profile-first principle), (2) if true org splitting is required, choose between Regional Orgs pattern or Big Markets + Country Clusters pattern.
rec_multi_org.next_step: Proceed to org design pattern selection.

rec_regional_orgs.detail: Separate orgs by major region (EMEA, APAC, Americas, LATAM). Within each regional org, use profiles and sharing rules for country-level separation. Cross-region data needs handled by integration platform + data warehouse.
rec_regional_orgs.next_step: Define regional boundaries and cross-region integration requirements.

rec_single_org_confirmed.text: Single Org Feasible — All five gates passed.
rec_single_org_confirmed.detail: Single org is technically viable. Implement with: (1) Multiple profiles per LOB/country, (2) Strong governance (CoE + governance committee + architectural review board), (3) Tiered administration, (4) Proactive data archiving, (5) Storage planning for 3+ years including historical loads.
rec_single_org_confirmed.next_step: Design profile structure, governance model, and CoE charter.

regional_orgs.name: Regional Orgs
pros: Capacity synergies across countries within region
Cross-country collaboration by configuration — no interfaces required
Reports and dashboards across countries by configuration
cons: Strong governance and configuration management required
All data hosted in same instance within region
Regional admins have access to all regional data
Complex compliance and sharing rules needed

country_clusters.name: Big Markets + Country Clusters
country_clusters.example: US, DACH (Germany/Austria/Switzerland), France, UK, Iberia (Spain/Portugal), Small Markets pool
pros: Local admin teams with full control
